You are implementing ONE requirement in the Apache Hadoop source tree at /workspace (a real upstream repo checked out at an earlier state).

REQUIREMENT SLUG: atsv2-hbase-classpath-order
REQUIREMENT FILE: /workspace/requirements/atsv2-hbase-classpath-order.yaml   <-- READ THIS FIRST

The `title:` field names the real upstream Apache Hadoop JIRA / git commit. Your job is to reproduce that upstream change as faithfully as you can from the requirement text plus the code you find in the tree. Hidden tests derived from the real upstream commit will grade the result, so EXACT naming matters:
  * new/changed configuration keys and their default values (and their entries in *-default.xml)
  * new class / interface / method / field / metric names and their visibility
  * log message wording and format placeholders
  * behavioural details (return values, exception types, ordering, off-by-one boundaries)
If the requirement text names an identifier (class, method, config key, metric, constant), use that identifier verbatim.

HOW TO WORK
1. Read the requirement yaml. Note the JIRA id and the module it belongs to (HDFS / YARN / MAPREDUCE / HADOOP-common / tools).
2. Locate the real code with Grep/Glob. Read enough surrounding code (and the existing tests for it) to make a correct, idiomatic change.
3. Implement the change. Match the surrounding code style, license headers, checkstyle habits (2-space indent, 80-col-ish, final where used, LOG placeholders `{}`).
4. If the change adds a config key, also add it to the matching `*-default.xml` (hdfs-default.xml / core-default.xml / yarn-default.xml / mapred-default.xml) with a sensible description, and to the `DFSConfigKeys`/`YarnConfiguration`/etc. constants class the module uses. Some modules have a TestYarnConfigurationFields / TestHdfsConfigFields style test that requires the xml and the constant to agree - keep them in sync.
5. If the upstream change would have come with tests, add or extend the corresponding test class under the same module (src/test/java/...). Keep tests deterministic and cheap. Do not add tests that need network or a real cluster beyond the usual MiniDFSCluster/MiniYARNCluster idioms already used in that test file.
6. Do NOT run maven/mvn or cmake (there is no warm build environment; it wastes your time). Instead be rigorous by inspection: every symbol you reference must exist (grep to confirm), every new import must be needed and correct, braces/parens balanced, no stale references left behind. Re-read your own final diff (`git diff -- <your files>`) before finishing and fix anything sloppy.
7. Scope discipline: change ONLY what this requirement needs. Do not reformat unrelated lines, do not fix unrelated warnings, do not touch other subsystems. Other agents are concurrently implementing ~380 other requirements in this same working tree.

FORBIDDEN COMMANDS (they would destroy other agents' concurrent work): git checkout / switch / stash / reset / revert / clean / rebase / merge / cherry-pick, `git add -A` or `git add .` without an explicit pathspec, `git commit --amend`, `git rm` of files you did not create, and any `mvn`/`gradle` invocation.

WHEN YOUR IMPLEMENTATION IS COMPLETE - commit it yourself with exactly this shape (substitute the real repo-relative paths you touched, space separated, and keep the flock):

  cd /workspace && flock /tmp/hadoop-git.lock bash -c 'git add -A -- PATH1 PATH2 ... && git diff --cached --binary > requirement_patches/atsv2-hbase-classpath-order.diff && git commit -q -m "impl: atsv2-hbase-classpath-order" && git log --oneline -1 && wc -c requirement_patches/atsv2-hbase-classpath-order.diff'

Rules for that step:
  * List every file you created, modified or deleted as an explicit pathspec. Never a bare directory like `.`.
  * requirement_patches/atsv2-hbase-classpath-order.diff MUST come out non-empty (wc -c > 0). If `git commit` reports "nothing to commit", another agent already committed your lines: verify the requirement is genuinely satisfied in the working tree, then report that in your notes.
  * Do not touch requirement_patches/ for any other slug.
  * IMPORTANT - a previous interrupted run left some UNCOMMITTED work in this tree. Before you start, run `cd /workspace && git status --short` and inspect `git diff` for the files you expect to touch. If part or all of this requirement is already implemented in the working tree but not yet committed, do NOT redo it from scratch: review it critically, finish/correct anything missing or wrong, then stage exactly those paths and commit as above. That uncommitted work is yours to claim when it belongs to this slug.

FINALLY return ONLY a JSON object (this is your return value, not a message to a human):
{"slug":"atsv2-hbase-classpath-order","status":"done"|"partial"|"blocked","files":["..."],"committed":true|false,"patch_bytes":<int>,"summary":"<=3 sentences on what you changed","notes":"anything the orchestrator must know (conflicts, follow-ups, uncertainty)"}

title: YARN-11045. ATSv2 storage monitor fails to read from hbase cluster
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Clusters with ATSv2 enabled can fail to connect cleanly to HBase because the timeline-service dependencies lose precedence on the runtime classpath.

  ## Desired outcome

  The ATSv2 launch path should load its dedicated timeline-service libraries before the general YARN classpath so the HBase-compatible dependency set wins consistently.

  ## Acceptance signals

  ResourceManager and NodeManager processes with ATSv2 enabled can reach the HBase-backed timeline service without classpath-order failures.

  '

# The name of the script being executed.
HADOOP_SHELL_EXECNAME="yarn"
MYNAME="${BASH_SOURCE-$0}"

## @description  build up the yarn command's usage text.
## @audience     public
## @stability    stable
## @replaceable  no
function hadoop_usage
{
  hadoop_add_option "--buildpaths" "attempt to add class files from build tree"
  hadoop_add_option "--daemon (start|status|stop)" "operate on a daemon"
  hadoop_add_option "--hostnames list[,of,host,names]" "hosts to use in worker mode"
  hadoop_add_option "--loglevel level" "set the log4j level for this command"
  hadoop_add_option "--hosts filename" "list of hosts to use in worker mode"
  hadoop_add_option "--workers" "turn on worker mode"

  hadoop_add_subcommand "app|application" client "prints application(s) report/kill application/manage long running application"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "applicationattempt" client "prints applicationattempt(s) report"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "classpath" client "prints the class path needed to get the hadoop jar and the required libraries"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "cluster" client "prints cluster information"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "container" client "prints container(s) report"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "daemonlog" admin "get/set the log level for each daemon"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "envvars" client "display computed Hadoop environment variables"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "jar <jar>" client "run a jar file"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "logs" client "dump container logs"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "node" admin "prints node report(s)"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "nodemanager" daemon "run a nodemanager on each worker"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "proxyserver" daemon "run the web app proxy server"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "queue" client "prints queue information"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "registrydns" daemon "run the registry DNS server"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "resourcemanager" daemon "run the ResourceManager"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "fs2cs" client "converts Fair Scheduler configuration to Capacity Scheduler (EXPERIMENTAL)"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "rmadmin" admin "admin tools"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "router" daemon "run the Router daemon"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "schedulerconf" client "Updates scheduler configuration"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "scmadmin" admin "SharedCacheManager admin tools"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "sharedcachemanager" daemon "run the SharedCacheManager daemon"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "timelinereader" client "run the timeline reader server"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "timelineserver" daemon "run the timeline server"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "top" client "view cluster information"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "nodeattributes" client "node attributes cli client"
  hadoop_add_subcommand "version" client "print the version"
  hadoop_generate_usage "${HADOOP_SHELL_EXECNAME}" true
}

## @description  Default command handler for yarn command
## @audience     public
## @stability    stable
## @replaceable  no
## @param        CLI arguments
function yarncmd_case
{
===
      fi
      HADOOP_CLASSNAME=org.apache.hadoop.yarn.client.cli.TopCLI
      HADOOP_SUBCMD_ARGS=("$@")
    ;;
    *)
      HADOOP_CLASSNAME="${subcmd}"
      if ! hadoop_validate_classname "${HADOOP_CLASSNAME}"; then
        hadoop_exit_with_usage 1
      fi
    ;;
  esac
}

# let's locate libexec...
if [[ -n "${HADOOP_HOME}" ]]; then
  HADOOP_DEFAULT_LIBEXEC_DIR="${HADOOP_HOME}/libexec"
else
  bin=$(cd -P -- "$(dirname -- "${MYNAME}")" >/dev/null && pwd -P)
  HADOOP_DEFAULT_LIBEXEC_DIR="${bin}/../libexec"
fi

HADOOP_LIBEXEC_DIR="${HADOOP_LIBEXEC_DIR:-$HADOOP_DEFAULT_LIBEXEC_DIR}"
HADOOP_NEW_CONFIG=true
if [[ -f "${HADOOP_LIBEXEC_DIR}/yarn-config.sh" ]]; then
  # shellcheck source=./hadoop-yarn-project/hadoop-yarn/bin/yarn-config.sh
  . "${HADOOP_LIBEXEC_DIR}/yarn-config.sh"
else
  echo "ERROR: Cannot execute ${HADOOP_LIBEXEC_DIR}/yarn-config.sh." 2>&1
  exit 1
fi

# now that we have support code, let's abs MYNAME so we can use it later
MYNAME=$(hadoop_abs "${MYNAME}")

# if no args specified, show usage
if [[ $# = 0 ]]; then
  hadoop_exit_with_usage 1
fi

# get arguments
HADOOP_SUBCMD=$1
shift

if hadoop_need_reexec yarn "${HADOOP_SUBCMD}"; then
  hadoop_uservar_su yarn "${HADOOP_SUBCMD}" \
    "${MYNAME}" \
    "--reexec" \
    "${HADOOP_USER_PARAMS[@]}"
  exit $?
fi

hadoop_verify_user_perm "${HADOOP_SHELL_EXECNAME}" "${HADOOP_SUBCMD}"

HADOOP_SUBCMD_ARGS=("$@")

if declare -f yarn_subcommand_"${HADOOP_SUBCMD}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  hadoop_debug "Calling dynamically: yarn_subcommand_${HADOOP_SUBCMD} ${HADOOP_SUBCMD_ARGS[*]}"
  "yarn_subcommand_${HADOOP_SUBCMD}" "${HADOOP_SUBCMD_ARGS[@]}"
else
  yarncmd_case "${HADOOP_SUBCMD}" "${HADOOP_SUBCMD_ARGS[@]}"
fi

# It's unclear if YARN_CLIENT_OPTS is actually a useful
# thing to have separate from HADOOP_CLIENT_OPTS.  Someone
# might use it, so let's not deprecate it and just override
# HADOOP_CLIENT_OPTS instead before we (potentially) add it
# to the command line
if [[ -n "${YARN_CLIENT_OPTS}" ]]; then
  HADOOP_CLIENT_OPTS=${YARN_CLIENT_OPTS}
fi

hadoop_add_client_opts

if [[ ${HADOOP_WORKER_MODE} = true ]]; then
  hadoop_common_worker_mode_execute "${HADOOP_YARN_HOME}/bin/yarn" "${HADOOP_USER_PARAMS[@]}"
  exit $?
fi

hadoop_subcommand_opts "${HADOOP_SHELL_EXECNAME}" "${HADOOP_SUBCMD}"

# everything is in globals at this point, so call the generic handler
hadoop_generic_java_subcmd_handler
